answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring a costly, verifiable work bond before an agent can transact. Each new identity must lock a small deposit and complete attested tasks over time, building a reputation record that cannot be transferred. Like pigment settling into a surface, this history marks genuine participants, while a mirror check compares behavior across peers to expose clones acting in lockstep. Creating thousands of Sybils then demands real deposits and distinct histories, so at dawn of an attack the cost already exceeds the profit from fake votes or offers.
